newsitem.title: UK: Boeing superjet in UK safety probe - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Boeing superjet in UK safety probe - newspaper.

text.p: An investigation has been launched into the new generation of superjet used by British Airways after one began to roll mysteriously and had to return to London's Heathrow airport, the Independent newspaper said on Friday.

The Air Accidents Investigation Board, the British government's safety adviser, is investigating the incident involving the Boeing 777 after a team from the plane's manufacturers spent a week examining the jet but failed to reach a conclusion, said the paper.
BA flight 133, which was carrying 85 passengers to Jeddah in Saudi Arabia last October, was forced to return to Heathrow after being in the air for a little over two hours.
The article quoted a Boeing spokeswoman as saying: "There have been no other occurrences of the incident by BA or any other 777 operator around the world."
No one at British Airways was immediately available to comment.
The 777 was produced by Boeing about three years ago. British Airways ordered 15 and have an option to buy another 15 -- an order worth 2 billion pounds ($3.3 billion).
